articles.title: New Dawn Fades Play to Showcase Joy Division's Rise at Heywood Civic
articles.excerpt: The play New Dawn Fades, depicting the story of iconic band Joy Division, will be performed at Heywood Civic next month, highlighting their journey from local clubs to international fame.
articles.content_html:
Music fans can look forward to a theatrical portrayal of the rise of Joy Division when the play New Dawn Fades is staged at Heywood Civic next month. The production chronicles the journey of the legendary band, which formed in Salford in 1976, featuring key members such as vocalist Ian Curtis, guitarist Bernard Sumner, bassist Peter Hook, and drummer Stephen Morris.

New Dawn Fades tells the compelling story of Ian Curtis and his bandmates as they navigate the music scene of 1970s Manchester. The play captures the blend of humour, drama, and music that defined their ascent from local clubs to the brink of international success, all while Curtis grappled with the pressures of fame and personal struggles.

The band is best known for their influential sound and seminal tracks, including Atmosphere, which was recorded at Cargo Studios in Kenion Street, Rochdale. Tragically, Curtis died by suicide in 1980, but the remaining members went on to achieve further success with their subsequent band, New Order.

The performance at Heywood Civic promises to be a powerful tribute to Joy Division's legacy, offering audiences a chance to reflect on the impact of the band and the life of its frontman. Tickets for the show are expected to be in high demand, given the band's enduring popularity.
